newsitem.title: USA: Clinton visits Marine camp, salutes troops.
newsitem.headline: Clinton visits Marine camp, salutes troops.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday visited a Marine base to salute the troops on duty during the holidays, praising them for their courage and joining them in a mess hall meal.

Making his first domestic trip since winning re-election on Nov. 5, Clinton ate lunch in the base mess hall, sent an e-mail to a unit just deployed in the Mediterranean and visited with the families of soldiers overseas.

Camp Lejeune, a 230 square mile (595 square km) complex in North Carolina, is the base for 42,000 Marines and sailors, including the Air Contingency Force, a rapid reaction unit ready to spring into action on as little as four hours notice.

"For all of America, surely there is no greater gift at Christmastime than the peace and freedom we enjoy," Clinton said in a speech at the base gymnasium. "Because you are standing watch, we can raise our children in freedom."
"Because you are standing watch, those children can sleep without fear and wake up to the kinds of holidays we are about to celebrate," he added.
"Day in and day out, your sacrifice makes all this possible. It is your gift to your country. For all your fellow Americans, in a very real way, you make every day Christmas," Clinton said.
Clinton ate lunch with some members of the rapid reaction force who cannot go home for the holidays because they are on standby alert over Christmas and New Year's Day.

The president carried a plastic tray through the cafeteria line, asking for turkey, stuffing, barbecued chicken, a mix of vegetables and a roll. Seeing his plate piled high with food, he then had second thoughts.
"That's terrible. I shouldn't eat all this," he said. "I'll have to run another couple of miles tomorrow."
Wearing a red Santa pin on his lapel and a festive, rainbow striped tie, Clinton spent more than an hour in the cafeteria, which was festooned with coloured Christmas lights and banners.

Some of those dining with Clinton served in operations to protect U.S. citizens in Liberia last summer. Their unit also took part in the daring rescue of downed Air Force pilot Scott O'Grady from Serbian-controlled territory in Bosnia in 1995.
Clinton spent four and a half hours at the base, taking a moment to write an e-mail to a unit that was sent abroad last month and on Monday was on a ship pulling into Trieste, Italy.
"Thank you and all your troops for your service to our country. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year to all of you," Clinton said in the note.

Clinton, who will spend his fourth Christmas at the White House on Wednesday, also made time for a visit with volunteer social service workers, many of them spouses of Marines and sailors posted overseas.

The White House said the president had chosen the Marines to represent the men and women of all of the armed forces, and had come to thank them on behalf of the American people for their service to the country.
He was scheduled to returned to Washington late in the afternoon.
